concepts.title: Nouns and Pronouns
concepts.description: Nouns and Pronouns — part of the chapter on Parts of Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of nouns and pronouns
Step-by-step problem solving for nouns and pronouns
Real-world applications of nouns and pronouns

concepts.title: Verbs and Tenses
concepts.description: Verbs and Tenses — part of the chapter on Parts of Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of verbs and tenses
Step-by-step problem solving for verbs and tenses
Real-world applications of verbs and tenses

concepts.title: Adjectives and Degrees of Comparison
concepts.description: Introduction to words that describe or modify nouns and pronouns, including the rules for forming comparative and superlative degrees.
key_ideas: Identifying adjectives of quality, quantity, and number
Using positive, comparative, and superlative degrees correctly
Position of adjectives in a sentence

concepts.title: Adverbs and Modification
concepts.description: Understanding how adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs to express manner, place, time, or frequency.
key_ideas: Distinguishing between adjectives and adverbs
Adverbs of manner (how), place (where), and time (when)
Formation of adverbs using the '-ly' suffix

concepts.title: Prepositions of Time, Place, and Direction
concepts.description: Learning words that establish relationships between nouns/pronouns and other parts of the sentence regarding location, timing, or movement.
key_ideas: Common prepositions (in, on, at, under, between)
Differentiating between prepositions of time and place
Correct usage to avoid common grammatical errors

concepts.title: Conjunctions and Linking Words
concepts.description: Using connecting words to join words, phrases, or clauses together to form compound or complex sentences.
key_ideas: Coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or, so)
Subordinating conjunctions (because, although, if)
Using conjunctions to improve sentence flow and logic

concepts.title: Interjections and Part of Speech Identification
concepts.description: Recognizing words that express sudden emotion and applying knowledge of all eight parts of speech to analyze sentences.
key_ideas: Using interjections (Wow!, Alas!, Hurrah!) for expression
Punctuation rules for interjections
Identifying the correct part of speech for words based on context

concepts.title: Simple, Compound and Complex Sentences
concepts.description: Simple, Compound and Complex Sentences — part of the chapter on Sentence Structure.
key_ideas: Core principles of simple, compound and complex sentences
Step-by-step problem solving for simple, compound and complex sentences
Real-world applications of simple, compound and complex sentences

concepts.title: Subject and Predicate
concepts.description: Introduction to the two fundamental parts of every complete sentence: the person or thing doing the action (Subject) and the part that tells something about the subject (Predicate).
key_ideas: Identifying the 'who' or 'what' (Subject)
Identifying the action or state of being (Predicate)
The role of the verb in the predicate

concepts.title: Types of Sentences Based on Function
concepts.description: Categorizing sentences based on their purpose: making statements, asking questions, giving commands, or expressing strong emotion.
key_ideas: Declarative sentences (Statements)
Interrogative sentences (Questions)
Imperative sentences (Commands/Requests)
Exclamatory sentences (Strong emotions)

concepts.title: Word Order and Sentence Formation
concepts.description: Learning the correct arrangement of words (syntax) to create meaningful sentences, focusing on the Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) pattern.
key_ideas: Standard SVO (Subject-Verb-Object) pattern
Rearranging jumbled words to form meaning
Placement of adjectives and adverbs

concepts.title: Phrases and Clauses
concepts.description: Distinguishing between groups of words that form a complete thought (clauses) and those that do not contain a subject-verb unit (phrases). This is a foundation for understanding complex sentences.
key_ideas: Definition of a Phrase (no subject-verb pair)
Definition of a Clause (contains subject and verb)
Independent vs. Dependent Clauses

concepts.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
concepts.description: Rules ensuring that the subject and verb in a sentence match in number (singular vs. plural).
key_ideas: Singular subjects take singular verbs
Plural subjects take plural verbs
Handling collective nouns and compound subjects

concepts.title: Present, Past and Future — Simple, Continuous, Perfect
concepts.description: Present, Past and Future — Simple, Continuous, Perfect — part of the chapter on Tenses.
key_ideas: Core principles of present, past and future
Step-by-step problem solving for present, past and future
Real-world applications of present, past and future

concepts.title: Regular and Irregular Verb Forms
concepts.description: Identification and memorization of base forms (V1), past forms (V2), and past participles (V3) for regular and irregular verbs.
key_ideas: Regular verbs add '-ed' or '-d' to form the past tense
Irregular verbs change spelling completely (e.g., go -> went)
The three forms: Base, Past Simple, and Past Participle

concepts.title: Simple Present vs. Present Continuous
concepts.description: Distinguishing between habitual actions or universal truths (Simple Present) and actions happening at the moment of speaking (Present Continuous).
key_ideas: Using Simple Present for habits, routines, and facts
Using Present Continuous for ongoing actions right now
Identifying signal words: 'always/usually' vs. 'now/at the moment'

concepts.title: Simple Past vs. Past Continuous
concepts.description: Understanding the difference between completed past actions and actions that were in progress at a specific time in the past.
key_ideas: Simple Past describes completed actions at a specific time
Past Continuous describes background actions or interruptions
Using 'when' and 'while' to connect past events

concepts.title: Expressing Future Time: Will vs. Going To
concepts.description: Learning different ways to express future actions using 'will', 'shall', and 'going to' based on intent and prediction.
key_ideas: Using 'will' for instant decisions or predictions
Using 'going to' for planned actions or intentions
Understanding the auxiliary role of 'shall' in suggestions

concepts.title: Negative and Interrogative Structures
concepts.description: Constructing negative sentences and questions across different tenses using appropriate auxiliary verbs (do, does, did, will, have).
key_ideas: Using 'do/does/did' + not for Simple Present and Past negatives
Inverting subject and auxiliary verb to form questions
Ensuring main verbs return to base form when using 'did'

concepts.title: Active and Passive Voice
concepts.description: Active and Passive Voice — part of the chapter on Active-Passive Voice and Direct-Indirect Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of active and passive voice
Step-by-step problem solving for active and passive voice
Real-world applications of active and passive voice

concepts.title: Direct and Indirect Speech
concepts.description: Direct and Indirect Speech — part of the chapter on Active-Passive Voice and Direct-Indirect Speech.
key_ideas: Core principles of direct and indirect speech
Step-by-step problem solving for direct and indirect speech
Real-world applications of direct and indirect speech

concepts.title: Subject-Object Transformation
concepts.description: Understanding how the object of an active sentence becomes the subject of a passive sentence and the use of the agent marker 'by'.
key_ideas: Swap the positions of Subject and Object
The doer of the action moves to the end
Introduction of the preposition 'by' before the doer
Identifying transitive verbs required for passive voice

concepts.title: Verb Forms in Passive Voice
concepts.description: Rules for changing the main verb into the Past Participle (V3) form and selecting the correct auxiliary verb (is/am/are/was/were) based on tense.
key_ideas: Passive voice always uses the Past Participle (V3) form
Using 'is/am/are' for Simple Present passive
Using 'was/were' for Simple Past passive
Agreement of the auxiliary verb with the new subject

concepts.title: Reporting Verbs and Connectors
concepts.description: Learning how to remove inverted commas and use conjunctions like 'that' when converting direct speech to indirect speech.
key_ideas: Removal of inverted commas (quotation marks)
Changing 'said to' into 'told'
Using the conjunction 'that' to connect clauses
Identifying the reporting verb

concepts.title: Pronoun and Time Shifts
concepts.description: Rules for changing personal pronouns to match the reporter and converting words denoting nearness in time/place to distance (e.g., now to then).
key_ideas: First-person pronouns change according to the subject
Second-person pronouns change according to the object
Changing 'now' to 'then', 'here' to 'there'
Changing 'today' to 'that day', 'tomorrow' to 'the next day'

concepts.title: Tense Backshift in Indirect Speech
concepts.description: Understanding how to shift the tense of the reported speech back into the past when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
key_ideas: Simple Present becomes Simple Past
Present Continuous becomes Past Continuous
No tense change if the reporting verb is in Present or Future tense
Universal truths remain in Present tense

concepts.title: Unseen Passages and Note Making
concepts.description: Unseen Passages and Note Making — part of the chapter on Reading Comprehension.
key_ideas: Core principles of unseen passages and note making
Step-by-step problem solving for unseen passages and note making
Real-world applications of unseen passages and note making

concepts.title: Vocabulary and Context Clues
concepts.description: Techniques to deduce the meaning of unfamiliar words by analyzing the surrounding text rather than relying solely on a dictionary.
key_ideas: Using synonyms and antonyms in the sentence as clues
Identifying definitions or examples provided within the text
Using the general mood or tone of the passage to guess word meaning

concepts.title: Identifying Main Idea and Theme
concepts.description: Learning to distinguish between the central message of a passage and the supporting details used to explain it.
key_ideas: Finding the topic sentence in a paragraph
Distinguishing between major points and minor details
Summarizing the central theme in one or two sentences

concepts.title: Distinguishing Fact and Opinion
concepts.description: Developing critical reading skills to identify statements that can be proven true versus statements representing feelings or beliefs.
key_ideas: Identifying verifiable evidence (dates, numbers, historical events)
Recognizing signal words for opinions (believe, feel, best, worst)
Understanding author bias in a text

concepts.title: Inference and Deduction
concepts.description: Reading 'between the lines' to understand information that is implied by the author but not explicitly stated in the text.
key_ideas: Drawing conclusions based on evidence in the text
Predicting outcomes based on character actions
Understanding character traits through dialogue and behavior

concepts.title: Poetry Comprehension
concepts.description: Analyzing poetic texts to understand literal meaning, imagery, and basic poetic devices used to convey emotion.
key_ideas: Identifying rhyme schemes and rhythm
Understanding basic imagery (similes and metaphors)
Interpreting the mood or feeling of the poem

concepts.title: Letter, Essay and Article Writing
concepts.description: Letter, Essay and Article Writing — part of the chapter on Writing Skills.
key_ideas: Core principles of letter, essay and article writing
Step-by-step problem solving for letter, essay and article writing
Real-world applications of letter, essay and article writing

concepts.title: Message Writing
concepts.description: Learn to draft short, informal messages to convey important information when direct communication is not possible, focusing on brevity and clarity.
key_ideas: Format: Date, Time, Salutation, and Sender
Conveying the core information concisely
Using indirect speech to report telephone conversations

concepts.title: Notice Writing
concepts.description: Understand how to write formal notices for school boards or public displays to announce events, lost and found items, or appeals.
key_ideas: Standard format: Box, Issuing Authority, Date, Heading
The 5 Ws: What, Where, When, Who, Whom
Adhering to word limits (usually 50 words)

concepts.title: Diary Entry
concepts.description: Develop the skill of recording personal experiences, feelings, and reactions to daily events in a creative and reflective manner.
key_ideas: Using first-person perspective ('I')
Informal and expressive tone
Format: Date, Day, Time, and Signature

concepts.title: Picture Composition
concepts.description: Practice observing visual cues in an image and translating them into a coherent paragraph or story using descriptive language.
key_ideas: Observation of details (characters, setting, action)
Using descriptive adjectives and prepositions
Logical sequencing of sentences

concepts.title: Story Writing
concepts.description: Learn to construct a narrative story based on given outlines, hints, or moral themes, ensuring a logical flow from beginning to end.
key_ideas: Developing a plot from an outline
Character and setting description
Providing a suitable title and moral
